author: Thomas à Kempis
title: That it is profitable to Communicate often

notes.text: (1) Psalm lxviii. 10. (2) Psalm lxxxvi. 4. (3) Matthew xv. 32. (4) Genesis viii. 21. (5) Psalm cxlvii. 5.

verses.text: Behold I come unto Thee, O Lord, that I may be blessed through Thy gift, and be made joyful in Thy holy feast which Thou, O God, of Thy goodness hast prepared for the poor.(1) Behold in Thee is all that I can and ought to desire, Thou art my salvation and redemption, my hope and strength, my honour and glory.
verses.modernizedText: See, I come to You, O Lord, that I may be blessed through Your gift and made joyful in Your holy feast, which You, O God, in Your goodness have prepared for the poor.(1) See, in You is all that I can and ought to desire; You are my salvation and redemption, my hope and strength, my honor and glory.

verses.text: Therefore rejoice the soul of Thy servant this day, for unto Thee, O Lord Jesus, do I lift up my soul.(2) I long now to receive Thee devoutly and reverently, I desire to bring Thee into my house, so that with Zacchaeus I may be counted worthy to be blessed by Thee and numbered among the children of Abraham.
verses.modernizedText: Therefore make the soul of Your servant rejoice this day, for to You, O Lord Jesus, I lift up my soul.(2) I long now to receive You devoutly and reverently; I desire to bring You into my house, so that with Zacchaeus I may be counted worthy to be blessed by You and numbered among the children of Abraham.

verses.text: My soul hath an earnest desire for Thy Body, my heart longeth to be united with Thee.
verses.modernizedText: My soul has an earnest desire for Your Body; my heart longs to be united with You.

verses.text: Give me Thyself and it sufficeth, for besides Thee no consolation availeth.
verses.modernizedText: Give me Yourself and it is enough, for besides You no consolation avails.

verses.text: Without Thee I cannot be, and without Thy visitation I have no power to live.
verses.modernizedText: Without You I cannot exist, and without Your visitation I have no power to live.

verses.text: And therefore I must needs draw nigh unto Thee often, and receive Thee for the healing of my soul, lest haply I faint by the way if I be deprived of heavenly food.
verses.modernizedText: Therefore I must draw near to You often and receive You for the healing of my soul, lest I faint by the way if deprived of heavenly food.

verses.text: For so Thou, most merciful Jesus, preaching to the people and healing many sick, didst once say, I will not send them away fasting to their own homes, lest they faint by the way.(3) Deal therefore now to me in like manner, for Thou left Thyself for the consolation of the faithful in the Sacrament.
verses.modernizedText: For You, most merciful Jesus, preaching to the people and healing many sick, once said, I will not send them away fasting to their own homes, lest they faint by the way.(3) Deal with me now in the same manner, for You left Yourself in the Sacrament for the consolation of the faithful.

verses.text: For Thou art the sweet refreshment of the soul, and he who shall eat Thee worthily shall be partaker and inheritor of the eternal glory.
verses.modernizedText: For You are the sweet refreshment of the soul, and whoever eats You worthily will be a partaker and inheritor of eternal glory.

verses.text: Necessary indeed it is for me, who so often slide backwards and sin, so quickly wax cold and faint, to renew, cleanse, enkindle myself by frequent prayers and penitences and receiving of Thy sacred Body and Blood lest haply by too long abstinence, I fall short of my holy resolutions.
verses.modernizedText: Indeed it is necessary for me, who so often slip backward and sin, and so quickly grow cold and faint, to renew, cleanse, and kindle myself by frequent prayers and acts of penitence and by receiving Your sacred Body and Blood, lest through too long an abstinence I fall short of my holy resolutions.

verses.text: For the imaginations of man’s heart are evil from his youth,(4) and except divine medicine succour him, man slideth away continually unto the worse.
verses.modernizedText: For the imaginations of the human heart are evil from youth,(4) and unless divine medicine helps, a person continually slips toward what is worse.

verses.text: The Holy Communion therefore draweth us back from evil, and strengtheneth us for good.
verses.modernizedText: Holy Communion therefore draws us back from evil and strengthens us for good.

verses.text: For if I now be so negligent and lukewarm when I communicate [or celebrate], how should it be with me, if I receive not this medicine, and sought not so great a help?
verses.modernizedText: For if I am now so negligent and lukewarm when I communicate [or celebrate], how would it be with me if I did not receive this medicine or seek so great a help?

verses.text: [And though I am not every day fit nor well prepared to celebrate, I will nevertheless give diligent heed at due season, to receive the divine mysteries, and to become partaker of so great grace].
verses.modernizedText: [And though I am not every day fit or well prepared to celebrate, I will nevertheless take diligent care in due season to receive the divine mysteries and become a partaker of such great grace].

verses.text: For this is the one principal consolation of a faithful soul, so long as it is absent from Thee in mortal body, that being continually mindful of its God, it receiveth its Beloved with devout spirit.
verses.modernizedText: For this is the one principal consolation of a faithful soul, as long as it is absent from You in a mortal body: that, continually mindful of its God, it receives its Beloved with a devout spirit.

verses.text: Oh wonderful condescension of Thy pity surrounding us, that Thou, O Lord God, Creator and Quickener of all spirits, deignest to come unto a soul so poor and weak, and to appease its hunger with Thy whole Deity and Humanity.
verses.modernizedText: Oh, wonderful condescension of Your pity surrounding us, that You, O Lord God, Creator and Giver of life to all spirits, deign to come to a soul so poor and weak and satisfy its hunger with Your whole Deity and Humanity.

verses.text: Oh happy mind and blessed soul, to which is granted devoutly to receive Thee its Lord God, and in so receiving Thee to be filled with all spiritual joy!
verses.modernizedText: Oh, happy mind and blessed soul, to which it is granted devoutly to receive You, its Lord God, and in receiving You to be filled with all spiritual joy!

verses.text: Oh how great a Lord doth it entertain, how beloved a Guest doth it bring in, how delightful a Companion doth it receive, how faithful a Friend doth it welcome, how beautiful and exalted a Spouse, above every other Beloved, doth it embrace, One to be loved above all things that can be desired!
verses.modernizedText: Oh, how great a Lord it entertains, how beloved a Guest it brings in, how delightful a Companion it receives, how faithful a Friend it welcomes, how beautiful and exalted a Spouse, above every other Beloved, it embraces—One to be loved above all things that can be desired!

verses.text: Oh my most sweet Beloved, let heaven and earth and all the glory of them, be silent in Thy presence; seeing whatsoever praise and beauty they have it is of Thy gracious bounty; and they shall never reach unto the loveliness of Thy Name, Whose Wisdom is infinite.(5)
verses.modernizedText: Oh, my most sweet Beloved, let heaven and earth and all their glory be silent in Your presence, since whatever praise and beauty they have comes from Your gracious bounty; and they will never reach the loveliness of Your Name, whose Wisdom is infinite.(5)
